issues.legal_issue: A law regulating the contractual relationship between real-estate promoters and purchasers falls within the concurrent fields of contracts and transfer of property, rather than the state field of industry.
material_facts: The state enactment regulated the contractual relationship between promoters and purchasers and provided for their rights, obligations, and remedies.
The state enactment substantially overlapped with a parliamentary enactment regulating the same relationship.
The state relied on the state legislative field of industry, but withdrew that contention during the hearing.
issues.conclusion: The court held that both enactments were, in pith and substance, referable to the concurrent fields of contracts and transfer of property, and that the state enactment was not a law on industry.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied Entries 6 and 7 of List III and Entry 24 of List II of the Seventh Schedule. It relied on Tika Ramji v State of Uttar Pradesh, Calcutta Gas Co. (Proprietary) v State of West Bengal, and ITC Ltd. v Agricultural Produce Market Committee for the principle that, in the constitutional context, industry means the process of manufacture or production and does not extend to the subject matter specifically assigned to other entries.

predicates.constitutional_validity_challenge_to_sta: A party challenged the constitutional validity of a state enactment.
predicates.state_law_regulates_promoter_purchaser_c: The state enactment regulates contractual rights, obligations, or remedies between real-estate promoters and purchasers.
predicates.state_law_does_not_regulate_manufacture_: The state enactment does not regulate the process of manufacturing or producing goods.
predicates.state_law_falls_within_concurrent_contra: The enactment is classified within the concurrent fields concerning contracts and transfer of property.

issues.definition: When a challenged state enactment regulates promoter-purchaser contracts rather than manufacture or production, it falls within the concurrent contract and property fields.

issues.legal_issue: A state enactment may be repugnant to a parliamentary enactment on a concurrent subject because of direct conflict, occupation of the whole field, or regulation of the same subject matter.
material_facts: The state and parliamentary enactments substantially overlapped in regulating the relationship between promoters and purchasers.
The enactments also differed on matters including parking, the scope of force majeure, the regulatory authority’s functions, and compensation adjudication.
The state enactment had not received presidential assent.
issues.conclusion: The court restated that repugnancy under Article 254 may arise from direct inconsistency, an exhaustive parliamentary code, or state and parliamentary laws regulating an identical subject; a state law is void to the extent of repugnancy, subject to the constitutional rule concerning presidential assent.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied Article 254(1) and (2), explaining that repugnancy may arise from irreconcilable conflict, Parliament’s intention to occupy the whole field, or overlapping regulation of the same subject. It emphasized considering both the text and context of the parliamentary enactment and that repugnancy is not the first choice where harmonisation is possible. It relied on Zaverbhai Amaldas v State of Bombay, Tika Ramji v State of Uttar Pradesh, Deep Chand v State of Uttar Pradesh, M Karunanidhi v Union of India, State of Orissa v M.A. Tulloch, Hoechst Pharmaceuticals Ltd. v State of Bihar, State of Kerala v Mar Appraem Kuri Company Ltd., and Innoventive Industries Ltd. v ICICI Bank.

rule.if: constitutional_conflict_review and not state_law_received_presidential_assent and (direct_irreconcilable_conflict or parliamentary_law_is_exhaustive_code or both_laws_regulate_identical_subject)

predicates.constitutional_conflict_review: A court is reviewing whether a state enactment conflicts with a parliamentary enactment on a concurrent subject.
predicates.state_law_received_presidential_assent: The state enactment received presidential assent in the circumstances specified by the constitutional rule for state laws on concurrent subjects.
predicates.direct_irreconcilable_conflict: The provisions produce conflicting legal results on the same facts such that compliance with one requires disobedience of the other.
predicates.parliamentary_law_is_exhaustive_code: The parliamentary enactment, considered in its text and context, is intended to provide a complete and exhaustive code on the subject.
predicates.both_laws_regulate_identical_subject: The state and parliamentary enactments regulate the same subject matter rather than distinct, merely allied matters.
predicates.state_law_yields_to_parliamentary_law_to: The state enactment gives way to the parliamentary enactment to the extent the two are repugnant.

issues.definition: In a constitutional conflict review, an unassented state enactment yields to parliamentary law to the extent that the laws irreconcilably conflict, the parliamentary law exhaustively covers the field, or both laws regulate the identical subject.

issues.legal_issue: A parliamentary real-estate regulatory scheme does not displace state and local laws governing land development and construction approvals.
material_facts: The parliamentary enactment referred to competent authorities, sanctioned plans, local laws, and planning areas.
State and local bodies governed matters such as permissible land use and development, construction standards, and the issuance of commencement, completion, and occupancy certificates.
The parliamentary enactment assigned implementation and regulatory functions to the appropriate government, including the state government for state matters.
issues.conclusion: The court held that the parliamentary enactment recognized and did not supplant state enactments governing permissible land use, construction norms, and local development regulation.
issues.legal_principle: The court relied on the parliamentary enactment’s definitions and scheme, including sections 2, 20, and 54, and on Entry 5 of List II concerning local government. It reasoned that references to competent authorities, local laws, sanctioned plans, and local certificates showed that Parliament left municipal and local regulation of construction activity in place.

predicates.real_estate_regulation_interacts_with_lo: The regulatory scheme concerns real-estate projects whose development is also governed by local laws.
predicates.parliamentary_scheme_recognizes_local_au: The parliamentary scheme refers to competent local authorities and approvals issued under local laws.
predicates.local_laws_govern_land_use_or_constructi: Local laws govern permissible land use, construction requirements, or development approvals.
predicates.local_development_regimes_remain_operabl: The local laws governing development and construction continue to operate alongside the parliamentary real-estate regulation.

issues.definition: Where a real-estate regulatory scheme recognizes local authorities and local development approvals, the local development regime remains operable.
